# Get-ZbxAlert

## SYNOPSIS

Gets the alerts that actions sent or ran.

## SYNTAX

### All (Default)


## DESCRIPTION

An alert is a message or a remote command an action sent or ran for an event, with its recipient, status and any error. The Get-ZbxAlert cmdlet reads them with alert.get: all of them up to -Limit, by id with -Id or from the pipeline, or with the whole alert.get selection in -Filter. -Group, -Host, -Action and the other object filters narrow the result to the alerts of the objects given, each a name, an id or a piped object. It writes ZabbixAlert objects, with their related objects when a -Select switch asks for them, or, with -CountOutput, the number of matches; it needs a connection made with Connect-ZbxServer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Get the alerts an action sent

```powershell
Get-ZbxAlert -Action 'Notify on disaster' | Select-Object AlertId, SendTo, Subject, Status, Error
```

-Action takes an action's name, id or object. Each ZabbixAlert is one message (or command) the server sent, with its recipient, status and any error.

### Example 2: Get the latest alerts about a host, with the media type used

```powershell
Get-ZbxAlert -Host 'web-01' -SelectMediaTypes -SortField clock -SortOrder Descending -Limit 10 |
    Select-Object Time, SendTo,
        @{ n = 'Media'; e = { $_.MediaTypes.Name } }, Status
```

-Host narrows to alerts about the host's events; sort by clock, newest first, and keep ten. -SelectMediaTypes adds the media type to each alert.

### Example 3: Find alerts that failed to go out

```powershell
Get-ZbxAlert -Limit 100 -SortField clock -SortOrder Descending | Where-Object Status -EQ Failed |
    Select-Object AlertId, SendTo, Error
```

Status is an enum on the record; failed alerts carry the reason in Error (here: the 'Mail relay' media type is disabled).
